title: Bangladesh sends border troops into Hasina's home district as Awami League protests turn violent
dek: Supporters of the banned party burned police vehicles in Gopalganj ahead of the first anniversary of her death sentence. They have called a lockdown for Thursday, and Dhaka wants India to hand her over.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Bangladesh has sent Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) troops and armoured vehicles into Gopalganj, the home district of former prime minister Sheikh Hasina, after supporters of her banned Awami League set a police vehicle on fire and clashed with police, as the party marks the first anniversary on Tuesday of the death sentence passed on her in absentia. The government has warned of tough action if the unrest spreads, and the party has called a "lockdown" for Thursday, 19 November.

The trouble puts India in the middle again. Ms Hasina has lived in India since she fled Dhaka in August 2024, she has said she will return to Bangladesh in December, and Dhaka wants New Delhi to hand her over. India says Bangladesh's extradition request is being examined under established legal procedures.

## What happened

On Sunday, hundreds of activists carrying machetes and spears took to the streets in Gopalganj, set an armoured police vehicle on fire and damaged a police outpost, according to reports citing officials. Protesters also set fire to a memorial to the July 2024 uprising that drove Ms Hasina from power, according to one report. The unrest has been building for a week: on 10 November, police said activists of the Awami League, its banned student wing the Bangladesh Chhatra League and affiliated groups set a police pickup van on fire and clashed with officers in Tungipara, Ms Hasina's ancestral home, who fired tear gas and rubber bullets, and protesters blocked the Dhaka-Khulna highway with burning wood and tyres, according to reports. No deaths in Gopalganj have been confirmed.

Reports differ on the size of the deployment: one said the home ministry ordered 10 BGB platoons into the district under the "In Aid to Civil Power" framework, with armoured personnel carriers and drones; others said six platoons were in place, three sent on 10 November and three more on Sunday, alongside police, the Armed Police Battalion and Ansar. The district's deputy commissioner and police superintendent were moved out on Sunday.

Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed said on Sunday night that the Awami League was trying to organise rallies centred on Gopalganj, that law enforcement was handling the situation patiently, and that it would act lawfully if the party crossed the line, according to reports. Unnamed government officials said the party was being incited "from abroad" and that the government wanted to avoid using force, because any death would let the Awami League present itself as a victim; they did not name a country. Brigadier General Mahmud Hasan, the BGB's Jessore region commander, said sabotage harming lives or property would not be tolerated.

## Background

The Awami League announced a five-day programme on 13 November leading up to 17 November, the first anniversary of the verdict of Bangladesh's International Crimes Tribunal, which sentenced Ms Hasina to death in absentia for crimes against humanity over the crackdown on the 2024 protests. She rejects the verdict as politically motivated. Earlier this month a wave of bus burnings and crude-bomb attacks, which police blamed on the Awami League, hit Dhaka and other districts. Prime Minister Tarique Rahman's government has refused Ms Hasina a passport. Foreign Minister Shama Obaid Islam on Monday denied a report that India had set conditions for an extradition, saying no such discussions had taken place, according to reports.

## Why it matters for India and Bengal

Unrest in Bangladesh is felt first along West Bengal's 2,217 km border with the country. Relations are already strained: a consular dialogue planned for this month in Dhaka has been postponed, and the Ganges water-sharing treaty, which governs the flow at Farakka, expires on 12 December with no renewal agreed. A return attempt by Ms Hasina from Indian soil, or violence around Thursday's lockdown, would add to the pressure on New Delhi to state its position on her.

## What happens next

- Tuesday, 17 November: anniversary of the tribunal's verdict
- Thursday, 19 November: Awami League "lockdown"
- 12 December: Ganges water treaty expires
- December: Ms Hasina's stated date for returning home
